_comment: FusionAuth tenant password policy mapped to the Amazon SP-API human-account
baseline (SP_API_REGISTRATION_REMEDIATION.md, controls 1-11).
TEMPLATE ONLY. Contains no secret and no tenant identifier. Apply with
PATCH /api/tenant/{tenantId} using an API key supplied from the operator's
environment -- never from this file, never from Git.
REQUIRES FusionAuth >= 1.63.0 (MINIMUM_FUSIONAUTH_VERSION, ADR-021):
`validateOnLogin`/`onLoginValidation` and the login-Id rejection setting
below do not exist in earlier versions. Applying this to an older release
silently drops the unsupported fields -- verify the version first.
COMMUNITY (UNLICENSED) ONLY. Verified 2026-08-26 against FusionAuth's
plans/premium-features pages: everything Amazon's controls 1-11 need is in
the free Community plan. Licensed features are deliberately absent --
`breachDetection` (Premium) was removed from this template on 2026-08-26,
and email/SMS MFA (paid) stay disabled below. Do not add a licensed field:
on a Community instance it fails or is ignored, and it would quietly break
the LICENSE_COST = $0 premise of ADR-021/ADR-031.

failedAuthenticationConfiguration._comment: Control 11: lockout at or below 10 failed attempts.

_comment: Control 10: MFA for all accounts. FusionAuth enables the methods here;
enforcement for every user is a separate step -- see the verification
procedure in IDENTITY_DEPLOYMENT_FUSIONAUTH.md. Enabling a method is
not the same as requiring it, and must not be evidenced as such.
RS256 only. interfaces/api/auth.py refuses every other algorithm,
including 'none' and any symmetric one, to close JWT algorithm
confusion. Key ids are assigned per tenant at deploy time.

control_8_minimum_password_age.note: Set on the tenant object alongside the rules above; kept separate here only because it sits outside passwordValidationRules in the Tenants API.

note: Amazon requires rejecting any part of the user's name. FusionAuth >=1.63.0
natively rejects only the configured login identifier, which is a distinct
field from firstName/lastName in FusionAuth's own data model.
This template does NOT close the gap and must not be cited as closing it.
The only mechanism that would inspect the plaintext password against the
name is a custom proxy in front of FusionAuth's APIs -- that is custom
authentication, which CLAUDE.md forbids. Resolution is an organizational
compensating control with disclosed residual risk, or Amazon's answer to
the clarification submitted in SP_API_REGISTRATION_REMEDIATION.md sec.21.
